disclaimer: AI research over the covered universe — not advice, not a recommendation. Cross-check every claim in the primary source before acting.

pitches.thesis: Q2 revenue up 92.8% y/y drove a +22.65% excess 3-day reaction, and FY guidance was raised again.
pitches.rationale: Palantir's Q2 revenue hit $1,935.5M (+92.8% y/y), and the stock's 3-day reaction was +22.65% excess to SPX — one of the sharpest post-earnings moves in the covered universe. Management raised FY2026 revenue guidance to $8.150-8.158B and lifted the U.S. commercial revenue floor to "in excess of $3.424 billion" (134%+ y/y growth), alongside a raised FY adjusted free cash flow range of $4.5-4.7B. Q3 guidance was also initiated at $2.160-2.164B revenue.
risks: Cash fell 11.4% q/q to $2,030.0M after $3.505B of marketable-securities purchases in the quarter — a liquidity-mix shift not explained in the release.
Management's headline $9.2B cash-plus-Treasuries figure doesn't reconcile with balance-sheet cash ($2.030B) plus marketable securities ($7.379B) = $9.409B, a roughly $200M unexplained gap.

pitches.thesis: EPS beat on higher realized oil pricing drove a +17.97% excess 3-day move even as revenue missed consensus.
pitches.rationale: APA's Q2 diluted EPS of $2.11 beat the $1.87 consensus estimate (+12.77%), and the stock's 3-day reaction was +17.97% excess to SPX. Revenue of $2,373M came in below the $2,428M estimate, so the beat was price- not volume-driven: realized oil price rose 50% y/y to $98.24/bbl while oil volumes fell 10% y/y. Management raised FY U.S. oil production guidance to 123,000 b/d and lifted the 2026 cost-savings target to $500M from $450M.
risks: Net debt remains $3.3B despite $673M of bond repayment in the quarter.
The EPS beat leaned on a 50% y/y realized-price gain rather than production growth — a reversal in oil prices would remove the driver behind the quarter's strength.

pitches.thesis: Revenue and EPS both beat, margins expanded, and the trend signal points to continued double-digit growth.
pitches.rationale: Airbnb's Q2 revenue of $3,608M beat the $3,575.6M consensus by 0.91%, and EPS of $1.37 beat $1.24886 by 9.70%. The stock's 3-day reaction was +21.75% excess to SPX, and the ranking's trend component shows +31.15% on next-quarter revenue estimate versus this quarter's actual. Adjusted EBITDA rose 21% y/y to $1.261B (35% margin, +1pt y/y), and Q3 revenue is guided to $4.69-4.77B (15-17% y/y growth).
risks: Net income was boosted by a one-time $77M tax benefit tied to newly published prior-year tax guidance, inflating the +27.1% y/y net income growth figure.
Total cash fell 7.8% y/y to $6.821B while short-term investments rose $1.294B, a liquidity mix shift alongside continued Reserve Now, Pay Later expansion.

pitches.thesis: Delivery guidance raised to 65-70k units and EBITDA loss narrowed, though the 3-day pop reversed within a week.
pitches.rationale: Rivian's Q2 diluted EPS of -$0.63 beat the -$0.77637 consensus by 18.85%, and the 3-day reaction was +15.57% excess to SPX. Management raised FY2026 delivery guidance to 65,000-70,000 units (from 12,194 delivered in Q2) and narrowed the FY adjusted-EBITDA loss outlook to -$1.8B to -$2.0B while cutting capex guidance to $1.7-1.8B. Notably, the d1 (-0.76%) and w1 (-3.75%) excess returns show the initial pop faded, leaving only the 3-day window positive.
risks: Net loss widened to -$833M q/q because Q1 FY2026 had booked a one-off $506M gain on the Mind Robotics deconsolidation that didn't recur.
A July 2026 offering (75M shares plus 11.25M over-allotment at $15.50/share, ~$1,317M net proceeds) isn't yet reflected in the Q2-end balance sheet — undisclosed dilution ahead.

pitches.thesis: Stock rallied +15.41% excess despite a GAAP loss, as the market focused on bitcoin-per-share growth, not EPS.
pitches.rationale: MicroStrategy posted a GAAP net loss of $8,219.6M (-$24.45 diluted EPS) driven by an $8.32B unrealized bitcoin fair-value markdown, yet the stock's 3-day reaction was +15.41% excess to SPX. The market appears to be pricing bitcoin-per-share (+5% q/q) and USD Reserve (+12% q/q to $2.4B) over GAAP earnings. Convertible debt fell 18% q/q to $6.71B after repurchasing $1.50B face value of notes at an 8% discount, and bitcoin holdings grew 11% q/q to 846,000 BTC.
risks: Cash fell 22.4% q/q to $1.71B after the $1.38B note-repurchase outlay, while share count rose 5.6% q/q on $2.95B of ATM equity issuance — ongoing dilution.
Shareholders' equity fell 34.9% y/y to $30.89B and accumulated deficit swung to $15.20B, both driven by the bitcoin markdown — earnings remain fully hostage to BTC price swings.

pitches.thesis: Eighth straight quarter of 60%+ revenue growth, with international revenue growing faster than the U.S.
pitches.rationale: Reddit's Q2 revenue grew 61.1% y/y to $804.9M — the eighth consecutive quarter above 60% growth — and the stock's 3-day reaction was +15.21% excess to SPX. International revenue grew 84% y/y versus 56% y/y domestically, DAUq rose 18% to 130.3M, and ARPU rose 36% to $6.18. Management guided Q3 revenue to $860-870M (47-49% y/y) and Adjusted EBITDA to $385-395M (63-67% y/y).
risks: Operating cash flow fell 16.1% q/q to $262M despite higher net income, a sequential decline the filing doesn't decompose.
Cost of revenue rose 53.2% y/y ($70M) on higher hosting usage, only partly offset by hosting-price efficiencies — a cost line growing faster than the 50bp gross-margin gain.

pitches.thesis: Revenue re-accelerated to +7.5% y/y and the 1-month excess reaction ran to +54.45%, the largest in the top 12.
pitches.rationale: ManpowerGroup's Q2 revenue grew 7.5% y/y (6% constant-currency) to $4,860.2M, and while the 3-day reaction was +13.32% excess to SPX, the 1-month excess reaction reached +54.45% — the largest sustained move among the top-ranked names. Management issued first-time Q3 EPS guidance of $0.96-1.06, including a roughly 2-cent unfavorable FX impact and a 44% effective tax rate.
risks: Gross profit rose only 2.2% y/y versus 7.5% revenue growth because cost of services grew faster at 8.6% y/y — a margin-compression signal not itemized by mix or pricing.
Cash fell 19.7% q/q to $180.6M after $585.8M of long-term debt repayment, while short-term debt rose $363.8M q/q to $476.2M.

pitches.thesis: FY guidance reaffirmed and a 45.1GW backlog through 2030 offset a y/y revenue decline from contract terminations.
pitches.rationale: First Solar's Q2 revenue fell 3.7% y/y to $1,056.2M on customer contract terminations, yet Adjusted EBITDA rose 14.9% y/y to $643.6M and the 3-day reaction was +14.24% excess to SPX. Management reaffirmed full-year 2026 guidance unchanged and issued first-time Q3 Adjusted EBITDA guidance of $625-775M. The company cited a 45.1GW contracted backlog extending through 2030 and surpassing 100GW of cumulative module sales.
risks: Revenue decline was driven "primarily by lower revenue from customer contract terminations" — a direct hit to the top line, not a comp effect.
Cash fell to $1.7B from $2.8B at year-end 2025 on seasonal working-capital needs and South Carolina facility capex.

pitches.thesis: Revenue hit $41.5B and forward guidance jumped again on new multi-year Strategic Customer Agreements in AI memory.
pitches.rationale: Micron's Q2 revenue reached $41,456M, and the stock's 3-day reaction was +21.73% excess to SPX (Nasdaq-100 benchmark). Management guided the next quarter's revenue to $50.0B +/- $1.0B and GAAP diluted EPS to $30.73 +/- $1.00 — a step-change tied explicitly to "new multi-year Strategic Customer Agreements" intended to improve pricing durability. Operating cash flow was $25.39B and cash rose to $25.0B from $13.9B, with a $0.15/share dividend declared.
risks: No analyst consensus estimate was present on the shard or in the release for this quarter's revenue, so this quarter's beat/miss magnitude isn't independently verifiable from the data on file.
The stored source link originally pointed to an unrelated 8-K (a board appointment filed 2026-06-09), not the earnings release — verify figures against the primary filing.

pitches.thesis: Lifyorli launch spend drove SG&A up 51% y/y, but the market still pushed shares up 25.63% excess over 1 day.
pitches.rationale: Corcept's Q2 revenue was $256.1M, and the stock's day-1 reaction was +25.63% excess to SPX, with the 3-day excess at +14.24%. Management gave no quantitative forward guidance, only qualitative language that R&D and SG&A expense will be higher in 2026 than 2025. SG&A rose 51.0% y/y to $156.9M on commercialization spend for both Hypercortisolism Products and the newly launched Lifyorli.
risks: Revenue growth was partly offset by a lower-priced generic mix from authorized-generic Hypercortisolism sales.
No share buybacks occurred in H1 2026 versus $130.5M repurchased in H1 2025, signaling a capital-return pullback alongside the step-up in launch spending.

pitches.thesis: Revenue and EPS beat consensus, but the EPS beat leaned on a $195M FX/derivative gain, not underlying growth.
pitches.rationale: Booking Holdings' Q2 revenue of $7,352M beat the $7,188M consensus by 2.28%, and EPS of $2.54 beat $2.43766 by 4.20%; the 3-day reaction was +10.10% excess to SPX. Management guided Q3 revenue growth to 4-6% and raised expected Transformation Program annual run-rate savings to approximately $650M by end of 2027. The EPS beat was driven mainly by a $195M FX/derivative gain on Euro-denominated debt (versus a $961M year-ago loss) — Adjusted EPS grew only 15% y/y on an underlying basis.
risks: Equity deficit deepened to -$10,783M (down 62% y/y) as $7,758M of six-month buybacks exceeded net income.
Long-term debt rose 18.1% q/q to $18,180M on $2,975M of new H1 debt issuance, and the quarter's EPS beat leaned on a non-operating currency swing rather than operating growth.

pitches.thesis: Revenue fell 7.6% y/y on reimbursement headwinds, yet FY guidance was raised to $835-875M and shares rallied.
pitches.rationale: Inspire Medical's Q2 revenue fell 7.6% y/y to $200.6M on U.S. coding/reimbursement headwinds, yet the stock's day-1 reaction was +21.04% excess to SPX. Management raised FY2026 revenue guidance to $835-875M and introduced adjusted diluted EPS guidance of $1.05-1.45, alongside a new "Project Horizon" initiative targeting approximately $30M of annualized reinvestment capacity.
risks: Revenue decline was driven by U.S. coding/reimbursement headwinds, a disclosed and ongoing regulatory risk to the domestic business.
Effective tax rate spiked to 89.9% (from -54.0% a year earlier) on a stock-comp tax shortfall — a volatile, non-operational item that could distort future EPS comparisons.
